why_this_addendum_exists: The prior review verified build commit fb4186e77612e6c81bdab819a78b9b79457edde9. self_correction.prior_statement: The offline claim was confirmed statically: the only socket reference in the entire package is socket.gethostname(). There is no HTTP client, no URL fetch, and no outbound call path anywhere in the implementation.
self_correction.status_at_prior_commit_fb4186e: TRUE AS WRITTEN. At fb4186e there was genuinely no network code.
self_correction.status_at_pinned_commit_39f1f40: NO LONGER TRUE. control_tower/drive_google.py (236 lines, new) performs real outbound HTTP via urllib.request.urlopen at line 83 and urllib.request.Request at line 99. Anyone relying on the prior sentence to conclude the pinned build cannot reach the network would be wrong.
self_correction.what_survives_unchanged: The dependency-free property holds. urllib is standard library, so third-party dependencies remain zero and the build still runs on the Windows workstation with nothing installed but Python.
compensating_controls_verified_this_run: The live Drive surface is opt-in behind an explicit --drive flag. It is not the default.
--drive additionally requires DBX_DRIVE_ACCESS_TOKEN to be set.
The import is lazy. cli.py imports GoogleDriveClient inside the --drive branch, with the stated intent that an offline run never even loads the network code.
audit refuses to run at all if selftest does not pass first, so the network path is unreachable on an unproven build.
canary is documented as the fast offline subset with no network of any kind.

empirical_proof_of_isolation.method: Ran the audit subcommand in-process without --drive, then inspected sys.modules for any module matching drive_google.
empirical_proof_of_isolation.result: drive_google was NOT present in sys.modules. Audit returned exit 2 as expected.
empirical_proof_of_isolation.verdict: OFFLINE_ISOLATION_CONFIRMED - the network module is never loaded without the explicit flag. This is an executed check, not a reading of the source.

reverification_at_pinned_commit.shim_gaps_found_and_closed: The strict stdlib shim initially lacked monkeypatch.delenv and excinfo.value, both of which the new Drive test file uses. Both surfaced as ERRORS rather than as false passes, which is the behaviour the shim was designed for, and both were implemented before the run was accepted. The committed shim now carries them.
reverification_at_pinned_commit.live_drive_leg_still_unproven: The --drive path was deliberately NOT exercised. Doing so would require a real access token and would put this unauthorized host on the live control surface. The 31 new tests exercise the client against in-process response doubles, which proves its request construction, error handling, and redaction logic but does not prove a real round trip against Google.

independent_corroboration_of_CT_RETIRE_0.claim: At the pinned commit the control kernel has no concept of a retired command; derive_authority grants authority on the retired Gate 0 command purely because it still sits in the pinned 01_QUEUED folder.
independent_corroboration_of_CT_RETIRE_0.independent_check_performed: Searched the whole package for retire, spent, revoked, denylist, and blocklist; read derive_authority; searched cli.py for Gate0Runner and any claim path.
independent_corroboration_of_CT_RETIRE_0.result: CONFIRMED. No retired-command concept exists anywhere in the package. derive_authority grants on folder membership by pinned ID alone. cli.py exposes only selftest, canary, and audit, and never constructs a runner or claim path.
independent_corroboration_of_CT_RETIRE_0.assessment: The other lane's characterisation is accurate and its severity rating is fair. This is a latent defence-in-depth gap, not an active exposure: nothing reachable from run_control_tower.bat can claim a command. The protection is topological rather than enforced, so it would silently stop holding the moment a caller wires the claim path. The proposed cure was correctly not applied, since applying it would move the branch tip the owner has pinned.
independent_corroboration_of_CT_RETIRE_0.reviewer_note: Independent corroboration matters here because the finding was self-reported by the lane that wrote the code it concerns.
